questions.text: All activities and patterns exhibited by animals before, during, and after mating to ensure successful reproduction and offspring survival are collectively referred to as
questions.explanation: Reproductive behaviour encompasses all activities related to mating and offspring survival.

questions.text: A male bird singing a complex song to attract a female is an example of what type of courtship display?
questions.explanation: Singing is an auditory signal used to attract mates.

questions.text: The bright, colourful plumage of a peacock used to attract a mate is a form of
questions.explanation: The peacock's plumage is a visual display for attracting mates.

questions.text: The release of pheromones by female insects to attract males from a distance is an example of
questions.explanation: Pheromones are chemical signals used for communication.

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary function of courtship behaviour?
options: To increase competition and aggression between males
To ensure that mating occurs only between members of the same species
To reduce the population size of a species
To test the physical strength of potential mates
questions.answer: To ensure that mating occurs only between members of the same species
questions.explanation: Courtship behaviour helps in species recognition, preventing interbreeding.

questions.text: Courtship behaviour helps in the synchronization of reproductive physiology between partners. This means it helps to ensure that
options: Both partners are the same age
Gametes are released at the same time
The partners are from the same species
The partners are of the same size
questions.answer: Gametes are released at the same time
questions.explanation: Synchronization ensures that gametes are released simultaneously for successful fertilization.

questions.text: A mating system where one male forms a pair bond with one female for at least one breeding season is known as
questions.explanation: Monogamy is a mating system where one male pairs with one female.

questions.text: Which of the following animals is a well-known example of a monogamous species?
questions.explanation: Eagles are known to be monogamous, often pairing for life.

questions.text: A pride of lions, consisting of one dominant male and several females, is an example of which mating system?
questions.explanation: Polygyny is a mating system where one male mates with multiple females.

questions.text: The mating system where one female mates with multiple males is called
questions.explanation: Polyandry is a mating system where one female mates with multiple males.

questions.text: In a polygynous mating system, there is often intense competition among males. This is because
options: Females are more aggressive than males
Fewer males get the opportunity to mate with multiple females
All males get an equal chance to mate
Males are responsible for raising the young
questions.answer: Fewer males get the opportunity to mate with multiple females
questions.explanation: Competition arises because only a few dominant males get to mate with many females.

questions.text: A major disadvantage of the promiscuous mating system is
options: High parental investment from both parents
questions.explanation: Promiscuity increases the risk of sexually transmitted diseases.

questions.text: The mating system observed in chimpanzees and bonobos, where no lasting pair bonds are formed, is
questions.explanation: Chimpanzees and bonobos exhibit promiscuous mating with no lasting pair bonds.

questions.text: The majority of fish species exhibit minimal parental care because they
options: Produce a large number of offspring (eggs) with external fertilization
questions.answer: Produce a large number of offspring (eggs) with external fertilization
questions.explanation: Fish produce many eggs externally, so parental care is minimal.

questions.text: In seahorses, a unique form of parental care is observed where
options: The female guards the eggs in her mouth
The male carries the fertilized eggs in a brood pouch
Both parents build a complex nest
The female feeds the young with a special milk
questions.answer: The male carries the fertilized eggs in a brood pouch
questions.explanation: Male seahorses carry fertilized eggs in a brood pouch.

questions.text: Mouthbrooding, as a form of parental care in some fish like tilapia, involves
options: The parent building a nest from mud and saliva
The parent carrying the fertilized eggs and young in its mouth for protection
The parent feeding the young with regurgitated food from its mouth
The parent using its mouth to fan water over the eggs
questions.answer: The parent carrying the fertilized eggs and young in its mouth for protection
questions.explanation: Mouthbrooding involves carrying eggs and young in the mouth for protection.

questions.text: The midwife toad is famous for its parental care behaviour in which
options: The female carries the eggs embedded in her skin
The male wraps the fertilized egg strings around his hind legs
The female builds a foam nest for the eggs
The male broods the eggs in his vocal sac
questions.answer: The male wraps the fertilized egg strings around his hind legs
questions.explanation: The male midwife toad carries egg strings around his hind legs.

questions.text: Poison dart frogs exhibit a high level of parental care by
options: Transporting tadpoles on their backs to water-filled plants
Producing milk to feed their young
Incubating their eggs in underground burrows
questions.answer: Transporting tadpoles on their backs to water-filled plants
questions.explanation: Poison dart frogs carry tadpoles on their backs to water-filled plants.

questions.text: Altricial birds, such as robins, hatch as
options: Helpless, blind, and featherless young requiring intensive care
Fully feathered and mobile young that can feed themselves
Independent young that leave the nest immediately
Young that are cared for only by the father
questions.answer: Helpless, blind, and featherless young requiring intensive care

questions.text: Precocial birds, like chickens and ducks, have young that are
options: Born helpless and require constant feeding
Relatively mature and mobile from the moment of hatching
Cared for exclusively by the male parent

questions.explanation: log₈p = (log₂p)/(log₂8) = n/3 = m, so n = 3m.

questions.text: The equation 5^(2x) - 26(5^x) + 25 = 0 has roots:
questions.explanation: Let y = 5^x. Then y² - 26y + 25 = 0, giving y = 1 or y = 25. So 5^x = 1 or 5^x = 25, hence x = 0 or x = 2.

questions.text: If log₁₀(x² - 5x + 7) = 0, find the values of x.
questions.explanation: log₁₀(x² - 5x + 7) = 0 means x² - 5x + 7 = 1, so x² - 5x + 6 = 0, giving x = 2 or x = 3.

questions.text: Consider the statement: "If a number is prime, then it is odd." The contrapositive of this statement is:
options: If a number is odd, then it is prime.
If a number is not odd, then it is not prime.
If a number is not prime, then it is even.
If a number is even, then it is not prime.
questions.answer: If a number is even, then it is not prime.
questions.explanation: The contrapositive of 'If P then Q' is 'If not Q then not P'.

questions.text: Which of the following is logically equivalent to p → q?
questions.explanation: p → q is equivalent to ¬p ∨ q.

questions.text: Given that p ∨ q is true and p ∧ q is false, which of the following must be true?
options: p is true and q is false
p is false and q is true
p and q have opposite truth values
p and q are both false
questions.answer: p and q have opposite truth values
questions.explanation: p ∨ q true and p ∧ q false means one is true and the other is false.

questions.text: The statement (p ∧ ¬q) → r is false when:
options: p is true, q is false, r is false
p is true, q is true, r is true
p is false, q is false, r is true
p is false, q is true, r is false
questions.answer: p is true, q is false, r is false
questions.explanation: For (p ∧ ¬q) → r to be false, the antecedent must be true and the consequent false.

Invalid because it commits the fallacy of the undistributed middle
Valid because it is a categorical syllogism
Invalid because it affirms the consequent

questions.text: Lactation, or milk production, is a key feature of parental care in which class of vertebrates?
questions.explanation: Lactation is a defining feature of mammals.

questions.text: The extended period of juvenile dependency seen in mammals like elephants and primates is essential for

Social learning and the transmission of cultural behaviours
Reducing the energy cost for the mother
Ensuring that the mother can produce another offspring quickly
questions.answer: Social learning and the transmission of cultural behaviours

questions.text: Reproductive behaviours are important for species survival because they ensure

Species continuity and maintenance of population numbers
That only the strongest individuals are born
That species do not need to adapt to their environment
questions.answer: Species continuity and maintenance of population numbers

questions.text: The process by which parents transmit genetic characteristics to their offspring is known as

options: Was the first to study genes under a microscope
Conducted groundbreaking experiments on inheritance in pea plants
Proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection
questions.answer: Conducted groundbreaking experiments on inheritance in pea plants

questions.text: Alternative forms of the same gene, such as those for tallness (T) and shortness (t), are known as
questions.explanation: Alleles are alternative forms of a gene.

questions.text: Thread-like structures in the nucleus, composed of DNA and protein, that carry genes are called
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are thread-like structures that carry genes.

questions.explanation: Genotype is the genetic makeup of an organism.

questions.text: The observable physical or biochemical characteristics of an organism, such as height or blood group, constitute its
questions.explanation: Phenotype refers to observable characteristics.

questions.explanation: Homozygous means having two identical alleles.

questions.text: An organism with the genotype Tt for plant height is best described as

questions.text: Mendel's Law of Dominance states that

Genes for different traits are inherited independently
All traits are blended in the offspring

It is carried but masked in the heterozygotes and is expressed when two recessive alleles come together
It is a new trait created by crossing over

questions.text: Mendel's Law of Segregation explains that
options: Dominant alleles are always separated from recessive alleles
During gamete formation, the two alleles for a trait separate, so each gamete gets only one allele
All possible gametes are produced in equal numbers
Genes on the same chromosome always stay together

questions.text: The process by which parents transmit genetic characteristics to their offspring is known as
questions.explanation: Heredity is the transmission of genetic characteristics from parents to offspring.

questions.text: Gregor Mendel is regarded as the "Father of Genetics" because he
options: Was the first to study genes under a microscope
Conducted groundbreaking experiments on inheritance in pea plants
Proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection
questions.answer: Conducted groundbreaking experiments on inheritance in pea plants
questions.explanation: Mendel's experiments on pea plants laid the foundation for genetics.

questions.text: A segment of DNA on a chromosome that codes for a specific protein or trait is called a
questions.explanation: A gene is a segment of DNA that codes for a trait.

questions.text: Alternative forms of the same gene, such as those for tallness (T) and shortness (t), are known as
questions.explanation: Alleles are alternative forms of a gene.

questions.text: Thread-like structures in the nucleus, composed of DNA and protein, that carry genes are called
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are thread-like structures that carry genes.

questions.text: The genetic makeup of an organism for a particular trait, represented by letters such as TT, Tt, or tt, is its
questions.explanation: Genotype is the genetic makeup of an organism.

questions.text: The observable physical or biochemical characteristics of an organism, such as height or blood group, constitute its
questions.explanation: Phenotype refers to observable characteristics.

questions.text: An organism that possesses two identical alleles for a particular trait (e.g., TT or tt) is said to be
questions.explanation: Homozygous means having two identical alleles.

questions.text: An organism with the genotype Tt for plant height is best described as
questions.explanation: Tt is heterozygous because it has two different alleles.

questions.text: An allele that is expressed in the phenotype even when present in a single copy (heterozygous condition) is a
questions.explanation: Dominant alleles are expressed even in heterozygous condition.

questions.text: An allele that is only expressed phenotypically when two copies are present (homozygous recessive condition) is a
questions.explanation: Recessive alleles are only expressed in homozygous condition.

questions.text: The specific physical location of a gene on a chromosome is its
questions.explanation: Locus is the specific location of a gene on a chromosome.

questions.text: Mendel's Law of Dominance states that
options: In a heterozygote, one allele may mask the expression of the other
Genes for different traits are inherited independently
All traits are blended in the offspring
questions.answer: In a heterozygote, one allele may mask the expression of the other
questions.explanation: The Law of Dominance states that one allele can mask the expression of another.

questions.text: When Mendel crossed pure-breeding tall plants (TT) with pure-breeding short plants (tt), all the offspring in the F₁ generation were tall. This demonstrates the Law of
questions.explanation: The Law of Dominance explains why all F₁ were tall.

questions.text: The recessive trait that disappears in the F₁ generation reappears in the F₂ generation. This is because
options: It is altered by the environment
It is carried but masked in the heterozygotes and is expressed when two recessive alleles come together
It is a new trait created by crossing over
questions.answer: It is carried but masked in the heterozygotes and is expressed when two recessive alleles come together
questions.explanation: Recessive traits reappear when two recessive alleles combine.

questions.text: Mendel's Law of Segregation explains that
options: Dominant alleles are always separated from recessive alleles
During gamete formation, the two alleles for a trait separate, so each gamete gets only one allele
All possible gametes are produced in equal numbers
Genes on the same chromosome always stay together
questions.answer: During gamete formation, the two alleles for a trait separate, so each gamete gets only one allele
questions.explanation: The Law of Segregation states that alleles separate during gamete formation.

questions.text: The 3:1 phenotypic ratio observed in the F₂ generation of a monohybrid cross is a direct result of the
options: Union of gametes carrying the same allele
questions.explanation: The 3:1 ratio is a result of the Law of Segregation.

questions.text: A cross that involves two pairs of contrasting characteristics, such as seed shape and seed colour, is called a
questions.explanation: A dihybrid cross involves two pairs of contrasting characteristics.

questions.text: The characteristic F₂ phenotypic ratio in a dihybrid cross, when both genes show complete dominance, is
questions.explanation: The F₂ phenotypic ratio in a dihybrid cross is 9:3:3:1.

questions.text: In the dihybrid cross RrYy × RrYy, what proportion of the offspring would be homozygous recessive for both traits (rryy)?
questions.explanation: The proportion of rryy is 1/16.

questions.text: Which of the following is an ore of aluminium?
questions.explanation: Bauxite is an ore of aluminium.

questions.text: The rate of a chemical reaction is expressed as
questions.explanation: Rate of reaction is change in concentration per unit time.

questions.text: Which factor does NOT affect the rate of a chemical reaction?
questions.explanation: Colour of reactants does not affect reaction rate.

questions.text: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by
questions.explanation: A catalyst decreases the activation energy.

questions.text: At equilibrium, the rate of forward reaction is the rate of backward reaction.

questions.text: According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing the temperature of an endothermic reaction will
questions.explanation: Increasing temperature shifts equilibrium in the endothermic direction (right).

questions.explanation: Boyle's law states that V ∝ 1/P at constant temperature.

questions.text: The volume occupied by one mole of any gas at s.t.p. is

questions.text: Which of the following is an endothermic reaction?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction.

questions.text: The enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states is called
questions.explanation: Enthalpy of formation is the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements.

questions.text: In an exothermic reaction, the heat content of the products is the reactants.
questions.explanation: In exothermic reactions, products have less heat content than reactants.

questions.text: How many moles are present in 18g of water? (H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of water = 18 g/mol, so 18g = 1 mole.

questions.text: The empirical formula of a compound containing 40% carbon, 6.67% hydrogen, and 53.33% oxygen is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: The empirical formula is CH₂O.

questions.text: What is the molar mass of CaCO₃? (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CaCO₃ = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100 g/mol.

questions.text: How many atoms are present in 2 moles of sodium?
questions.explanation: 2 moles × 6.02 × 10²³ = 1.204 × 10²⁴ atoms.

questions.text: A rite of passage marking entrance into a group or society is:

questions.text: The unwritten rules that define acceptable behavior in a society are:

questions.text: A West African historian and storyteller who preserves oral tradition is a:

questions.explanation: Vertex at x = 2, y = -3.

questions.explanation: Discriminant > 0 gives m < -4 or m > 4.

questions.text: A trader bought x items for ₦(x² + 10x) and sold them for ₦(2x² - 5x). If his profit was ₦240, find x.
questions.explanation: Profit = (2x² - 5x) - (x² + 10x) = x² - 15x = 240, so x = 16.

questions.text: A solid sphere of radius 9cm is melted and recast into a solid cylinder of height 12cm. Find the radius of the cylinder.

questions.text: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 12 cm is full of water. This water is poured into a cylindrical container of internal radius 8 cm. Find the height of water in the cylinder.
questions.explanation: Volume of hemisphere = volume of cylinder, so h = 18 cm.

questions.text: A sphere of radius 7 cm is dropped into a cylindrical vessel of radius 14 cm partly filled with water. Find the rise in water level when the sphere is completely submerged.
questions.explanation: Rise in water level = volume of sphere / area of cylinder = 7/3 cm.

questions.text: The surface areas of two spheres are in the ratio 16:25. Find the ratio of their volumes.
questions.explanation: Ratio of volumes = (ratio of radii)³ = (4/5)³ = 64/125.

questions.text: A hollow sphere has external radius 10 cm and internal radius 8 cm. Find the volume of material used.
questions.explanation: Volume of material = 4/3 π(R³ - r³) = 4/3 π(1000 - 512).
